## Lesson 3 — Read the one-port S11 response {#lesson-s11}

**Prerequisite:** run Lessons 1–2 in the aggregate Chapter Notebook.

`CircuitRun` seals this Plan for analysis and returns caller-owned Results in memory. The
frequency grid is an explicit 401-point request from 5.75 GHz through 6.25 GHz.

```{python}
#| id: ch1-prepare-direct-request
frequencies = np.linspace(5.75, 6.25, 401) * u.GHz
run = CircuitRun(
    plan=plan,
    storage="memory",
)
direct_spec = DirectSolveSpec(frequencies=frequencies)
```

```{python}
#| id: ch1-solve-baseline-s11
baseline_response = run.solve(
    run.original,
    direct_spec,
    parameters=ParameterSet(),
)
```

For phasor signs, output-row/input-column order, wrapped phase, and dB units,
see [Simulation conventions](../../../docs/concepts/simulation-conventions.qmd).

The public presentation shows both magnitude and phase from the returned typed
Result. For this ideal lossless one-port model, `|S11|` is approximately 0 dB
across the grid; the phase still carries the readable response feature. A
magnitude dip is therefore not a resonance definition for this example. The
fixed ±0.05 dB display range keeps floating-point roundoff from being visually
autoscaled into a false feature; it does not round or change the response data.
The phase is shown as returned, including its ordinary wrapped-phase
discontinuity; that jump is angle presentation, not a numerical failure. The
horizontal axis is displayed in GHz while the Result retains the original
frequency units. Phase is displayed in degrees.

```{python}
#| id: ch1-show-baseline-s11
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import display

response_plot = baseline_response.s.plot(magnitude="db")
magnitude_plot = go.Figure(data=[response_plot.data[0]])
phase_plot = go.Figure(data=[response_plot.data[1]])

for figure, component, unit in (
    (magnitude_plot, "magnitude", "dB"),
    (phase_plot, "phase", "deg"),
):
    figure.update_traces(
        xaxis="x", yaxis="y", line={"color": "#246398", "width": 2},
        hovertemplate="%{x:.6g} GHz<br>%{y:.6g} " + unit + "<extra></extra>",
    )
    figure.update_layout(
        template="plotly_white", autosize=True, height=340, showlegend=False,
        title={"text": f"S11 {component}", "x": 0.02, "xanchor": "left"},
        margin={"l": 78, "r": 24, "t": 55, "b": 62},
        paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
    )
    figure.update_xaxes(title_text="Frequency (GHz)", automargin=True)
    figure.update_yaxes(title_text=f"{component.capitalize()} ({unit})", automargin=True)
magnitude_plot.update_yaxes(range=[-0.05, 0.05])
display(magnitude_plot)
display(phase_plot)
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

Port 1 is `signal_in`; S11 is reflection at that same measurement Port.
